opening_message:
Ticket 1: Timothy Wallace (employee ID E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer. He requested admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so as a full-time employee without ownership, his maximum is write. Admin is above the maximum, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a contractor with basic security training per the Security DB. Contractors with basic training max out at read (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed). He requested admin to Payroll, which is above the max, so I recommend granting read.
reason: HR's database is authoritative for employment type: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Engineer, so admin is not permitted; his maximum is write. The requested level (admin) is above the maximum, so the maximum (write) is granted. The Security note's conflicting contractor status conflicts with the HR record; HR determines employment type, and even so, the granted level does not exceed any applicable cap.
